To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SADI is a simple, lightweight, fully standards-compliant design pattern for Web services; SADI enables the automatic discovery and composition of Web services; and SADI enables data generated by Web services to be explored in the same manner as static Semantic Web data.

the SADI design pattern, API and reference implementation significantly improves the ability of Semantic Web services to support the needs of end-users, and to be utilized by software in automated workflows.

the SADI design pattern is a simple, lightweight and standards-based approach to Web service design that enables the automatic discovery and chaining of services, and the dynamic creation of data resources from distributed, non-coordinated Web services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of interoperability standard that is both simple to implement, yet capable of supporting the most complex and dynamic of bioinformatics applications.
the creation of a lightweight, fully standards-compliant set of Semantic Web Service design patterns that simplify and automate the integration of distributed, heterogeneous resources.
the integration of Web Services and Semantic technologies, and we believe SADI represents an important step towards achieving this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SADI is an important step forward in the development of the Semantic Web, and that the Semantic Web will not reach its full potential without the inclusion of SADI services.
SADI is a significant step towards the realisation of a truly Semantic Web of Services.
SADI is the first Web services technology that has the potential to be adopted by the scientific community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SADI design-patterns, API and reference implementations provide a simple and intuitive way of exposing resources as Semantic Web services that is accessible to non-technical users, while providing a powerful mechanism for software to automatically discover and utilize these services.

, in addition to being an excellent fit for the biological domain, SADI is an excellent fit for any scientific domain where data is distributed across a large number of resources, and where data is often dynamically generated by those resources, rather than stored in a static repository.

the SADI design pattern and API provide a powerful, yet lightweight mechanism for the creation, discovery, and utilization of Web services that can dramatically improve the utility and interoperability of the bioinformatics community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by following simple best-practices, Semantic Web services can be deployed that are easy to use for biologists, and that are amenable to automatic discovery, chaining and analysis by software.
Semantic Web technologies are not only compatible with Web service technologies, but can greatly improve the ability of Web services to work together.

, by following a very simple set of standards-compliant best practices, the bioinformatics community will be able to realize the full power of the Semantic Web in the service-oriented computing domain.
